## How a recommendation is made

```
issue labels ──► lang/<key> + job/<key>        (hatsu:classify writes them)
repo kind/role + issue labels + jobs ──► domain (first matching rule wins)
(job, domain, language) ──► routing cell       (winner + runner-up, each an ALIAS)
alias ──► provider · model family · surface · tier ──► the name you type
job weights + counts + domain ──► effort       (low | medium | high | max)
```

1. **Two labels decide it.** `lang/` is what the work is written in (`swift`, `kotlin`, `typescript`, `csharp`, `prose`); `job/` is the kind of work (39 keys, below). `hatsu:classify` applies them; `direct` only reads them.
2. **The domain is derived, never labelled** — from the repository's kind and role, the issue's `bug` label and its jobs ([rules](#which-domain-am-i-in)).
3. **One cell per (job, language).** Every cell names a *winner* and a *runner-up* alias. A language column only exists where that language is routed differently; otherwise the shared `*` cell applies (and `prose` always reads `*`).
4. **An alias is stable; a version is not.** The alias names a provider, a model family and the Hatsu surface it runs on. The name you type comes from `nen/workflow.json` → `models.<surface>.<tier>`; the newest version is read live when `direct` runs, with the dated snapshot below as the fallback.
5. **No `job/` label, no recommendation** — undirectable: `direct` says so in one line and `build` continues on the current session.

## Which domain am I in?

Rules are checked in order; **the first match wins**.

| # | Domain | When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AI governance** (`aigov`) | nen repo classify reports kind process, or role canon |
| 2 | **Reusable library** (`library`) | nen repo classify reports kind library |
| 3 | **Cross-platform parity** (`parity`) | the issue carries job/parity, the marker job -- reached only in a product repository: rows 1 and 2 (a process or library repository) win first and keep their own table |
| 4 | **Maintenance & operations** (`maintenance`) | the issue carries the repository's bug kind label (a label named bug, or <ns>:bug), or it carries at least one job and every job it carries lists only maintenance phases |
| 5 | **Feature development** (`feature`) | otherwise |

*Hatsu and nen themselves are process / canon repositories, so work on them is always **AI governance**.* When a job has no phase in the derived domain, it routes on the first domain it does list, in this order: the derived domain, then maintenance, feature, library, aigov, parity — and `direct` names the substitution.

## How hard — the effort rule

**score = the highest job weight**, plus one for each of:

- three or more jobs
- two or more code languages (prose does not count)
- the derived domain is aigov

| Score | Effort |
|---|---|
| ≤ 2 | **low** |
| 3 | **medium** |
| 4 | **high** |
| ≥ 5 | **max** |

Job weights:

| Weight | Jobs |
|---|---|
| 4 | `requirements`, `architecture`, `api-design`, `security` |
| 3 | `discovery`, `analysis`, `orchestration`, `ux`, `integration`, `accessibility`, `integration-tests`, `ui-automation`, `performance`, `review`, `release`, `observability`, `bug-fix`, `migration`, `deprecation`, `prose-authoring`, `schema`, `evals`, `drift-review`, `parity` |
| 2 | `backlog`, `ui`, `implementation`, `unit-tests`, `ci-cd`, `triage`, `refactor`, `upgrades`, `machinery`, `documentation`, `adapters`, `onboarding`, `provisioning`, `delivery-ops` |
| 1 | `mechanical-edit` |

How each surface spells the level (`effort.surfaceMap`):

| Level | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Antigravity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | `low` | `low` | `low` | `low` |
| medium | `medium` | `medium` | `medium` | `medium` |
| high | `high` | `high` | `high` | `high` |
| max | `max` | `xhigh` | `high` | `high` |

Cursor and Antigravity have no top setting, so `max` reads `high` there — and a session already at `high` on them counts as matching.

## Several jobs or languages on one issue

Every (job, language) pair gets its own cell; one recommendation comes out:

1. **Winner** — the alias that wins the most pairs; a tie goes to the earlier alias in this order: `SEMANTIC_MAX` › `SEMANTIC_FRONTIER` › `EXECUTION_FRONTIER` › `VISUAL_ORCHESTRATOR` › `EXECUTION_VALUE` › `BALANCED_AUTHOR` › `VISUAL_FALLBACK` › `MECHANICAL_EDITOR` › `PR_QUALITY_REVIEW` › `PR_SECURITY_REVIEW`.
2. A review bot never wins: a pair it wins counts for the actionable alias after its arrow.
3. **Runner-up** — the alias with the next-most wins; if the winner won every pair, the most frequent runner-up across those pairs (same tie-break). If nothing else is left, *runner-up: none distinct*.
4. `prose` and an empty `lang/` read the shared `*` cell; `prose` never counts as a code language for effort.

| A SwiftUI feature with its tests<br><sub>repo kind `product`</sub> | `lang/swift` `job/ui` `job/implementation` `job/unit-tests` | Feature | 🟠 `sonnet` · Claude Code | 🟠 `opus` · Claude Code | **medium**<br><sub>weight 2 + three or more jobs</sub> | `claude --model sonnet (then /effort medium)` |
| A TypeScript bug fix<br><sub>repo kind `product`</sub> | `lang/typescript` `job/bug-fix` `job/unit-tests` `bug` | Maintenance | 🟠 `sonnet` · Claude Code | 🟠 `opus` · Claude Code | **medium**<br><sub>weight 3</sub> | `claude --model sonnet (then /effort medium)` |
| Designing a Kotlin library's public API<br><sub>repo kind `library`</sub> | `lang/kotlin` `job/api-design` | Library | 🟠 `opus` · Claude Code | 🟠 `fable` · Claude Code | **high**<br><sub>weight 4</sub> | `claude --model opus (then /effort high)` |

## Surfaces, restart lines and interactive equivalents

The actionable recommendation is always one of Hatsu's four surfaces. `direct` fills `<alias>` from `models` and `<level>` from the effort map — never a version.

| Surface | Restart line | Effort control | Model lookup | Interactive twin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | `claude --model <alias> (then /effort <level>)` | /effort low|medium|high|max | the harness's model picker (/model) lists the served aliases | the Claude desktop app or claude.ai, the same model family |
| **Codex** | `codex -m <alias> -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` | model_reasoning_effort low|medium|high|xhigh | codex debug models | ChatGPT's Codex web app or the Codex IDE extension, the same model family |
| **Cursor** | `cursor-agent --model <alias>` | the model's own thinking setting | cursor-agent --model help lists the served models | the Cursor IDE chat and Composer, the same model |
| **Antigravity** | `the Antigravity workspace with Model: <alias> on the lead` | the model's thinking budget (pro) -- no four-step dial | the workspace's model picker | the Antigravity IDE itself, or the Gemini app for a conversation |

Native IDE equivalents by language (offered beside the winner as the *interactive* row):

| Language | Native interactive option |
|---|---|
| Swift | Xcode's native integration (Apple Intelligence; ChatGPT and Claude where Xcode offers them) |
| Kotlin | Android Studio / IntelliJ (Gemini in Android Studio; Copilot where enabled) |
| TypeScript | VS Code or WebStorm with GitHub Copilot Chat, or the Cursor IDE |
| C# | Visual Studio with GitHub Copilot (Opus, Sonnet and Sol where the plan offers them) |
| Prose | the Claude desktop app or claude.ai |

## Where the version comes from

At run time `direct` reads the newest version of the recommended family — the surface's own lookup first, then the provider's model page, quoted with its URL and date. Only when neither can be read does it quote the snapshot above, **with its date (2026-10-04)**.

| Provider | Surface lookup | Model pages |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic | the Claude Code model picker (/model), read in-session | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview<br>https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview |
| openai | codex debug models | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog<br>https://openai.com/index/practical-guide-building-gpt-6/ |
| google | — | https://antigravity.google/docs/subagents<br>https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models |
| cursor | cursor-agent --model help | https://cursor.com/changelog<br>https://cursor.com/composer |
| copilot | — | https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models |

## Keeping this page true

```bash
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --write    # re-render after any registry, taxonomy or models edit
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --check    # exit 1 when this page is stale
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --verify   # every cell, fallback and example against nen direct resolve
```

A routing change is a registry edit through a PR, never an edit here; changing what an alias **means** is a maintainer ruling ([`ROSTER.md`](ROSTER.md) § *Rulings of 2026-10-04 — classify and direct*).
